name: Baga Kaloum
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Lamp, Frederick John. 2021 [2016]. Baga Tshi-Tem Dictionary (Guinea). PDF, Cataloging Africana. Front matter pp. 6-7.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About 40 entries tagged 'Bkl = Baga Kalum', nearly all copied from Koelle 1854/1963; states 'no dictionaries exist for these dialects'. Its 'accent generally falls on the initial syllable' remark (p. 7) concerns Baga Sitemu, not Kalum.

sources.citation: Arcin, André. 1907. La Guinée française: races, religions, coutumes, production, commerce. Paris: Challamel. Annexe II 'Observations linguistiques', §3 'Petit vocabulaire Baga', pp. 642-643. archive.org id laguinefrana00arci.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bare French-Baga wordlist (numerals pinn, parenn, passas, paânghlé, ktsamatt.. matching Koelle's Kalum forms pin, paren, pasas), no locality stated, no pronunciation or accent remark. The annex's one accent sentence (p. 631, 'il semble que l'accent tonique soit placé sur la dernière syllabe') is in §1 on the Mandé languages, not Baga.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald, Forkel, Robert, Haspelmath, Martin & Bank, Sebastian. 2025. Glottolog 5.3, languoid baga1271 'Baga Kaloum' (Bookkeeping).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry retired as spurious: 'The now extinct Baga Kaloum is attested in Koelle 1854 which shows they spoke the same language as the Baga Koga [bgo] (Dalby 1965, Voeltz 1996: 5-7)'. Zero descriptive references listed for baga1271.

sources.citation: Rochant, Neige. 2023. A bilectal grammar of Baga Pukur: an Atlantic language of Guinea. PhD thesis, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle. Ch. 1 pp. 15-16 and p. 229.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Not a description of Kalum. Lists 'The Baga Kalum, the first inhabitants of Conakry and its suburbs (Kaporo)' among seven Baga subgroups; Kalum, Koba, Kakisa, Sitemu, Mandori form one Mel subgroup; Berliner 2013 reports Baga Kalum, Koba and Kakisa/Sobané 'no longer speak their native language'. p. 229: the Baga group 'not known to be tonal'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English), 'Baga language' (with 'Baga Kaloum language' redirect), citing Wilson 1962 (SLLR 1), Wilson 2007, Fields-Black 2008, Hammarström 2015.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Kaloum 'extinct by the 1950s', code 'spurious'; 'The extinct Baga Kaloum and Baga Sobané peoples had spoken Koga and Sitemu, respectively'; Wilson 2007 (after Voeltz 1997): Baga Koba 'reportedly very similar to Baga Kaloum'.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana, or a comparative vocabulary of nearly three hundred words and phrases in more than one hundred distinct African languages. London: Church Missionary House. Introductory remarks p. [xv] (informant list, 'Fourth Group, 1. Baga') and orthographic key p. [xii]; wordlist columns 'D.1. Baga (of Kalum)'. archive.org scanned id polyglottaafrica00koel.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary attestation of Baga Kaloum (informant Stephen/'Ambre of Balanser opposite the Isles de Los, 'Kalum-Baga'). Koelle: 'There are three different Baga countries on the coast: the Kalum-Baga, to which Stephen belongs, the Rio-Pongas-Bagas, and the Rio-Nunez-Bagas. In the first two countries nearly the same language is spoken'. The key lists only "' the common sign for the accent, e.g., a, d." — accent marks on wordlist forms (not preserved by the scanned), no statement of where the accent falls.
